definition: Generative art is post-conceptual art that has been created (in whole or in part) with the use of an autonomous system.
details: An autonomous system in this context is generally one that is non-human and can independently determine features of an artwork that would otherwise require decisions made directly by the artist. In some cases the human creator may claim that the generative system represents their own artistic idea, and in others that the system takes on the role of the creator. "Generative art" often refers to algorithmic art (algorithmically determined computer generated artwork) and synthetic media (general term for any algorithmically generated media), but artists can also make generative art using systems of chemistry, biology, mechanics and robotics, smart materials, manual randomization, mathematics, data mapping, symmetry, and tiling. Generative algorithms, algorithms programmed to produce artistic works through predefined rules, stochastic methods, or procedural logic, often yielding dynamic, unique, and contextually adaptable outputs—are central to many of these practices.

explainer.lead: Generative art is made by giving part of the creative decision-making to an autonomous system. Instead of specifying every detail, the artist establishes a process that can determine features of the work, raising practical questions about authorship, control, and variation.

tiers.eli5: Imagine inventing rules for a drawing game and then letting a machine play it. You might choose the colours and basic rules, while the machine decides where each shape goes. The finished pictures are generative art because something other than you helped make the creative decisions.
tiers.practitioner: An implementation typically encodes predefined rules, stochastic methods, or procedural logic and lets the resulting system determine features of the artwork. Computation is common, but the same approach can use chemistry, biology, mechanics, robotics, smart materials, mathematics, data mapping, symmetry, tiling, or manual randomization. A key design choice is how much decision-making to delegate, since highly variable outputs can make artistic control and attribution less straightforward.
tiers.paperLevel: Generative art is post-conceptual art A created wholly or partly through an autonomous system S, where S is generally non-human and independently determines features that would otherwise require direct decisions by the artist. Algorithmic generation is a common case, using predefined rules, stochastic methods, or procedural logic, but autonomy can also arise through chemical, biological, mechanical, robotic, material, or manual processes. The framework leaves authorship open: the human may regard S as expressing their artistic idea, or may treat S itself as the creator.

explainer.example: An artist writes rules for placing tiled shapes, including a stochastic choice of colour and position. Running the algorithm produces a unique composition in which the artist chose the rules but did not directly decide every shape’s appearance or location.

usedIn.name: Algorithmic art
usedIn.detail: Computer-generated works whose features are determined algorithmically.

usedIn.name: Synthetic media
usedIn.detail: Media generated through algorithmic processes rather than fixed entirely by hand.

usedIn.name: Robotics and mechanics
usedIn.detail: Physical systems can autonomously determine aspects of an artwork.

usedIn.name: Chemistry and biology
usedIn.detail: Chemical or biological processes can serve as the generative system.

explainer.intuition: The artist designs or initiates a process rather than manually deciding every feature of the final piece. The process then exercises enough independence to make some artistic decisions itself.
howItWorks: The artist supplies an idea, rules, materials, or other starting conditions.
An autonomous system operates through rules, randomness, procedures, or physical processes.
The system independently determines some features of the work.
The resulting process or output becomes all or part of the artwork.
explainer.whyItMatters: Generative art expands art-making beyond fixed, manually specified objects to dynamic, varied, and context-sensitive outputs. It also makes the division of creative agency between artist and system an explicit part of artistic practice.
misconceptions: It does not have to be computer-generated.
Algorithmic generation does not require the artist to approve every output detail.
Using an autonomous system does not settle whether the artist or the system is the creator.
